newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-U.S. Robotics x2 sales strong.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-U.S. Robotics x2 sales strong.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp's sales of its recently shipped x2 high-speed modems and network hubs were "extremely strong" following a successful sales and marketing campaign, chief executive Casey Cowell said.

"Sales of x2 were incredibly strong on both the systems products and the client side or the end user products," Cowell said in a telephone interview. "They were extremely strong which is one of the reasons we saw a dramatic shift up in the gross margins overall."

Skokie, Illinois-based U.S. Robotics reported fiscal second quarter earnings of $0.77 a share excluding a one-time gain versus $0.55 a share last year. According to First Call, analysts' consensus estimate was $0.75 a share.
The company said gross margins for the quarter rose to 49.1 percent of net sales from 41.9 percent last year and 42.8 percent in its fiscal first quarter.
The company began shipping its x2 desktop modems in February.
The x2 technology allows users to connect to the Internet at speeds up to 56 kilobits per second over conventional telephone lines, or roughly twice as fast as today's standard modems.

There is no standard 56-K technology, so users must connect to a U.S. Robotics hub or another x2 modem to get the high speeds. The hub technology, used by Internet Service Providers, was available in March.
Cowell said the x2 rollout included stepped-up marketing and sales expenses in an effort to gain market share.
Cowell said x2 prices and margins will likely fall as 56-K competition increases. "But when that does happen, we feel we will be in a very strong market position," he said.

Cowell declined to comment on future earnings estimates. He said as U.S. Robotics had agreed to merge with 3Com Corp and expects the deal to close in June, the company does not expect to report separate results for its fiscal third quarter.
According to First Call, the consensus estimate for fiscal 1997 earnings is $3.27 a share.
Cowell said days of sales outstanding increased again in the quarter to 95 days, which shows how long it takes a company to collect receivables, but the company expects that number to trend downward.
"We expected to see it trend down to more acceptable levels (after second quarter)," Cowell said. "And based on results of this (third) quarter to date so far, that seems to be the case."
In after hours trade, U.S. Robotics shares were up one from Wednesday's close at 48.
